question.text: During the time interval 2 s ≤ t ≤ 6 s, an object moves along a straight path such that its velocity v and acceleration a (in m/s²) satisfy the relation v = 4/a m/s. Given that the velocity of the object is v = 6 m/s at the instant t = 2 s, calculate its acceleration at t = 3 s.
conditions: valid for time interval 2 s ≤ t ≤ 6 s

solution.approach: Write acceleration as dv/dt = 4/v, separate variables and integrate to get v(t), then compute a = 4/v at t = 3 s.

steps.text: Write acceleration as dv/dt and set it equal to the given relation.
Separate the variables and integrate both sides.
Use v = 6 m/s at t = 2 s to find the constant C.
Find v at t = 3 s from v²/2 = 4t + 10.
Find the acceleration at t = 3 s using a = 4/v.
steps.why_this_step: The acceleration is not constant here since it depends on v, so it must be re-evaluated at the new speed.

common_mistakes.text: Using the velocity given at t = 2 s directly in a = 4/v, getting a = 4/6 = 0.667 m/s² instead of solving for v at t = 3 s.
Writing the left side of ∫v dv as v instead of v²/2, so that v = 4t + C, gives v = 10 m/s at t = 3 s and a = 0.4 m/s².
